facts.statement: Arrudatitan was relatively gracile compared to other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: It was relatively gracile for a titanosaur.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPMA 12-0001-97, containing partial vertebrae, ribs, chevrons, a scapula, arm bones, and leg bones, was discovered in 1997 by Ademir Frare and his 12-year-old nephew in Cândido Rodrigues.
facts.quote: The holotype, MPMA 12-0001-97, which includes two partial posterior cervicals, fragments of several dorsals, parts of nine caudals, seven partial cervical ribs, twelve partial dorsal ribs, eight chevrons, a fragmentary scapula and arm bones, the left and partial right femur, the left ischium, and fragments; with other specimens known, such as the isolated middle caudal vertebra MPP 248, was discovered in 1997 by Ademir Frare and his 12-year-old nephew Luiz Augusto dos Santos Frare in a field in Cândido Rodrigues.

facts.statement: Fernando Novas briefly noted the size of the holotype in 2009.
facts.quote: In 2009, Fernando Novas briefly noted on the holotype, noting its size.

facts.statement: The species was initially assigned to the genus Aeolosaurus in 2011 as Aeolosaurus maximus.
facts.quote: MPMA 12-0001-97 was initially assigned to Aeolosaurus in 2011, when the species Aeolosaurus maximus was created by Santucci & De Arruda-Campos.

facts.statement: The genus Arrudatitan was erected in 2021 by Silva et al. after analyses showed the species did not belong in Aeolosaurus.
facts.quote: subsequent analyses, such as Silva et al. (2019) and Hechenleitner et al. (2020), found that Aeolosaurus maximus did not belong in the Aeolosaurus genus and so the new genus Arrudatitan was erected in 2021 by Silva et al.

facts.statement: Arrudatitan grew up to 15 meters long when fully grown based on the holotype.
facts.quote: Arrudatitan grew up to 15 m when fully grown, based on the size of the holotype.

facts.statement: The femur length of Arrudatitan is 1.55 meters.
facts.quote: The femur length of Arrudatitan is 1.55 m.

facts.statement: Arrudatitan is classified within the family Titanosauria.
Arrudatitan belongs to the family Aeolosauridae.
Arrudatitan is placed in the tribe Aeolosaurini.
The genus Arrudatitan was named by Silva Junior in 2021.
One cladistic analysis found Arrudatitan to be the sister group to Rinconsauria.
facts.quote: el primer análisis encontró que era hermano de Rinconsauria

facts.statement: Another cladistic analysis found Arrudatitan to be closely related to a clade consisting of Punatitan and other Aeolosaurus species.
facts.quote: el último encontró que estaba estrechamente relacionado con un clado formado por Punatitan y las otras dos especies de Aeolosaurus.

facts.statement: Arrudatitan lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 74 to 70 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, en el Campaniense, hace aproximadamente 74 a 70 millones de años, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The time range for Arrudatitan is from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species A. maximus was originally described in 2011 as Aeolosaurus maximus before being moved to its own genus in 2021.
facts.quote: The type species, A. maximus, was named and described in 2011 as a species of Aeolosaurus, but was separated into its own genus in 2021.

facts.statement: Based on the holotype, Arrudatitan reached a length of 15 meters when fully developed.
facts.quote: Arrudatitan creció hasta 15 metros cuando estaba completamente desarrollado, según el tamaño del holotipo.

facts.statement: The femur of Arrudatitan measures 1.55 meters in length.
facts.quote: La longitud del fémur es de 1,55 metros.
